branches.title: Mask selection as a side channel
branches.stage:

NO masked-image encoder trained, no real image data, no novelty or paper result. Previous mutual-information definitional correction remains in force. PRIMARY SOURCE + CODE AUDIT (Oct 27): Accepted CVPR 2023 AdaMAE already learns full-video-informed visible-token selection. Its released pretraining code embeds ALL input tokens and calls get_mask(x) before restricting the encoder to x[~mask] with positional embeddings. This establishes a possible position-information path but neither leakage in the pretrained model nor a test-time classifier effect. The previous intentional toy example cannot demonstrate novelty. Narrow to source/policy-specific conditional measurements with matched patch count and robust position-only/content-only/joint probes; do not call adaptive masking itself novel. SOURCE FEASIBILITY (Oct 27): AdaMAE CVPR 2023 official repository README links pretrained SSv2/K400 model-weight archives at GitHub release v1. This is a checkpoint availability CLAIM in the original README, not a tested, loaded sampler. Next verify release files contain trained sampling-network weights, exact code revision, licensing and shape compatibility. No weight download, probe or real video test. branches.question: Can a content-dependent adaptive sampler encode hidden-image information through selected patch positions, and does this bias masked-image learning?
branches.novelty: CORRECTION: the earlier I(Y; M | V) proposal is identically zero when V includes spatial positions of visible patches, since M is the complement of those positions. This is a definitional problem, NOT negative empirical evidence. Informative missingness (GRU-D), adaptive token selection (AdaMAE) and adaptive masking are established. The only plausible new claim concerns mask-policy-induced shortcut learning under carefully controlled sample selection; no novelty claim yet. CLOSEST ACCEPTED PRIOR ART: Bandara et al., AdaMAE (CVPR 2023) already trains a full-video-informed adaptive token sampler (https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2023/html/Bandara_AdaMAE_Adaptive_Masking_for_Efficient_Spatiotemporal_Learning_With_Masked_Autoencoders_CVPR_2023_paper.html). The reviewed open-source pretrainer (https://github.com/wgcban/adamae/blob/main/models/pretrain/vit.py) gets a full input embedding before sampling positions; this is architectural information flow, NOT observed semantic leakage or a novel masking policy. Avoid claiming general leakage or that downstream inference is affected.
branches.pilot:
Define S=visible position set, B=values of visible patches without their indices, and T=(S,B) as actual encoder input. Compare position-only S probe, content-only B probe, and S+B probe on a balanced synthetic dataset engineered so visible patch values are identical across labels while the adaptive policy uses unseen context to select blank positions. Compare fixed/random masks and a selector with no access to hidden context; hold count, grid, split and compute fixed. Then test whether a public MAE checkpoint's advantage survives masking-policy swaps and held-out inputs. Report I(Y;S|B) ONLY with B explicitly excluding position indices, not the invalid I(Y;M|T). This sanity example is not evidence of publication novelty. Toy CPU; actual pretrained model small GPU if needed. ACTUAL SCIENTIFIC NEXT STEP: on an independently held-out public image sample, keep count and identity of encoder/decoder fixed and compare a public pretrained MAE checkpoint under masking-policy swaps, including a selector without hidden-context access and a position-only probe. This CPU sanity control is not enough. SOURCE-PINNED NEXT GATE: Audit release/model weight access and freeze AdaMAE sampler and token embedder; separate video-source train, development and sealed test. Probe selected indices without content, position-stripped selected values, and joint values at identical visible count; negative controls random independent indices and index-permuted sampler output. Use a constructed held-fixed-visible-candidates hidden-region perturbation to test whether unseen content causally changes sampled positions; distinguish index-label correlation from additional information after accounting for sampled content. Screen <=2 CPU core-hours, zero GPU; no pretrained-model result yet.

For the source-only preflight, use the GitHub release API to pin checkpoint filename and length; next inspect open source constructor/load keys and license, then only if a justified sample size and runtime fit the CPU cap inspect/download exact binary. Hash checkpoint when authorized. No inference claim based on release metadata.
branches.stop: If the position-only control does not carry repeatable information on held-out inputs, or the shortcut has no measurable representation/downstream effect after policy controls, retire the performance-inflation claim. Review direct prior art before submitting. Stop if the apparent index-label effect disappears after matching visible content, random/index-permutation controls, or if the frozen released sampler cannot be run within the authorized cost; a source-level possible path alone is not a conference contribution.

branches.question: Without knowing which sources have matches at inference time, can an allocation policy learn both match-existence probability and last-positive-rank completion curves to improve complete-link retrieval among all source queries under fixed candidate count AND end-to-end wall time, versus QASP-style and progressive-ER baselines?
branches.novelty: The PACMMOD/SIGMOD 2025 Progressive ER formal objective maximizes progressive recall@N of verified PAIRS, assumes oracle pair verification and explicitly excludes verification time from reported runtime. QASP (Jul 2026) predicts recall of nearest-neighbor search as probes increase; nearest-neighbor recall is NOT recall of all semantically true entity links. The proposed completion event max_true_match_rank<=K differs from both losses, but this is not proof of novel algorithm. Distinct evaluation must include multi-positive sources (standard clean-clean datasets often assume within-source no duplicates), real full-pipeline runtime, calibrated completion prediction, and equal-budget strong baselines. Critical new gate (Oct 27): allocation over positive queries only is oracle information leakage unless positivity is inferable at inference. Estimate p_i*F_i(k) over all S1, assess null-query opportunity cost and incomplete ground truth. No new algorithm claimed. A new necessary CONTROL is randomized source-level monotone score offsets: a policy can redistribute budget across sources without changing their local candidate ranks or using any label. Neither stochastic prioritization (SPER) nor generic budgeted success curves are intrinsically novel. A learned all-link allocator must show more than what random budget concentration achieves at equal B. DATASET GATE: WDC Products EDBT 2024's official val/test subsets assign two offers per product, so its isolated test does not provide multi-positive complete-link recall; do not treat pairwise evaluation as a multi-link retrieval benchmark. Leipzig Music Brainz 20K offers CID-labeled multi-source groups but has synthetic perturbations and source-specific duplication assumptions. Novelty must generalize beyond generated duplicate examples, under sealed cluster-disjoint testing. Additional prior art: EDBT 2025 GraLMatch already evaluates group-level multi-source ER; a June 2026 batched-oracle preprint studies progressive cost-controlled group recovery; an October 2026 multilingual-company preprint distinguishes retrieval from final clustering. Claim novelty only for verified completion-aware allocation under a different cost model and end-to-end controlled evidence. ACCEPTED PRIOR ART: Alper (KDD 2026, DOI 10.1145/3770855.3817856) optimizes adaptive costly pair queries together with graph refinement on eight dirty-ER datasets. Generic cost-aware adaptive ER or clustered retrieval is not first here. Distinguish the proposed complete-link retrieval-at-fixed-candidate-cost objective and test against a faithful Alper comparator when its different LLM-query cost model can be normalized. Treat ambiguous Cora XML title tags as a label-audit parser warning, never as canonical bibliographic title ground truth. Additional accepted ICDE 2026 paper already identifies candidate generation and reproducibility as important end-to-end linker bottlenecks; Oct 2026 preprint already defines author-cluster lumping/splitting metrics. Neither is a new CC-04 contribution.
branches.pilot: NEXT: Audit and freeze a harder REAL-WORLD multi-positive entity dataset, with complete-link label assumptions explicitly tested. Preserve deterministic cluster-disjoint fit/calibration/test and include all zero-match queries in budget. Use Leipzig Music Brainz 20K only as a documented synthetic control: train-only IDF, frozen cosine scoring, matched candidate B, uniform, global-score, 16 predetermined source-offset seeds; add a degree-capacity upper bound showing that fixed-K cannot complete queries with more than K true links. On harder data evaluate fitted probability-of-completion versus strong global/top-B, randomized concentration, QASP/Progressive ER/SPER variants under full CPU cost and inference-available signals. Do not open the sealed Leipzig split or claim paper novelty during development. For real Cora citations (package by Steorts et al.), use original citation records and raw public pairwise gold, NOT unverified generated cora_gold_update labels. Audit clique closure, isolate singletons, independently inspect likely false negatives, freeze a cluster-disjoint split before models, include size-skew controls and cluster bootstrap. Classify Cora as a small real dirty-ER sanity/stress test, not an independent real multi-source benchmark. Require candidate-to-matcher-to-cluster outcome measurements, and stop if labels remain incomplete or a learned policy cannot improve over global-score and random allocation at equal end-to-end costs. NEW source-verified benchmark option: MaDI-Bench base Companies and Music integrate three real heterogeneous sources and have held-out labeled pairs and staged matching/fusion scorers; the released pair-label sets are NOT complete entity-cluster gold, and the end-to-end reference uses silver clusters. First perform train/dev-only label coverage and cluster-closure audit; do not measure all-links completeness against missing pair labels. Faithfully compare Alper on identical data only after fixing its eight-dataset runner overrides, cache accounting, and excluding embeddings/index construction from its reported elapsed-time field. Distinguish candidate budget from dollar-costed LLM oracle budget. First document the star-shaped labeled source-pair topology and group-disjointness of training/validation records; use only training and development for preprocessing, parameter selection and label-coverage audits. Freeze source IDs, candidate universe, source-offset seeds and full-cost policy before retrieval. Do not inspect official test outcomes. BOUNDED NEXT DATASET: inspect S2AND's source manifests and author-name block completeness before any CPU retrieval pilot; keep per-block cluster-disjoint train/calibration/test and distinguish single-corpus author disambiguation from natural multisource matching. Official public Arrow release is large (about 10.1 GiB); do not fetch it as a side effect of source scouting. For GraLMatch, reuse only released synthetic group data as a control, not inaccessible financial data. Exact next S2AND source-aware control: run label-only TRAIN metadata audit for cluster IDs spanning blocks, ID overlap across partitions, singleton/missing labels, and within-block closure; pin iteration order, seed, block type and split unit. Only then allow train/dev retrieval at equal costs. Do not treat cluster metrics as global all-source completion. PORTFOLIO PRIORITY: This is NOT the voice-related IndoML project. Never reuse audio event data as a record-linkage benchmark or infer ICDE fit from that project. Proceed only under independent, explicit data/IR scope.
branches.stop: If no reliable gain over strong global-score AND QASP/progressive baselines on a new sealed cluster-disjoint test, or if gain is due to incomplete annotations/model-selection leakage, retire standalone adaptive-allocation claim. Candidate-universe missing links cannot be repaired by reallocation. Also stop novel learned-allocation claim if it cannot beat an uninformed rank-preserving source-offset baseline on the prospectively sealed test. No novel algorithm inferred from artificial score perturbations. Do not interpret a single-positive-only official benchmark as evidence for multi-positive all-links completion. Stop any new-data claim if controls differ in candidate universe, annotation coverage, or information available at inference. New finding: When a simple global-score allocation already approaches candidate-oracle completion on synthetic duplicates, retire that dataset as primary method-novelty evidence and seek harder real-world independent annotations. Do not advertise the mathematically predetermined failure of K<true-link-count uniform retrieval as algorithmic discovery. MaDI base tasks cannot support an all-source completion claim without independently verified cross-source group labels, including non-anchor pairs. If label verification fails, pivot to the benchmark's official labeled-pair blocking/matching and fusion evaluation.

branches.question: Can detected event boundaries improve temporal retrieval or question answering at equal frame budget?
branches.novelty: Boundary-guided frame sampling predates this work (BMVC 2021), and long-video QA methods already curate query/event-relevant frames at fixed token budgets (Ground, Cover, and Refine 2026; MemoryCard 2026). Claiming first boundary-based QA sampling would be false. Narrower question: whether VIDEO-GENERIC GEBD boundaries, without text/query conditioning, have incremental QA value over equally dense semantic-event and query-aware selectors, and at what noise scale. NEW: RIDGE (Findings EMNLP 2026, 2026.findings-emnlp.1813) is accepted and directly studies derivative-informed region/boundary frame selection at fixed budgets without training. dKFD (arXiv:2609.33083) studies supervised pre/event/post allocation (preprint only). Neither generic temporal phase preservation nor query-score turning points are novel; isolate truly query-agnostic event boundaries and detector overhead.
branches.pilot: Fixed 16/32-frame budgets, one frozen video QA model. Compare uniform, random, GEBD oracle, predicted GEBD, semantically selected events, and matched query-aware selector. Lock all question annotations and timestamp window, report temporal-relation vs object-identity QA separately plus frame-selection oracle gap and detector cost. First run a small diagnostic on available annotated clips, then require a disjoint larger public set before a paper claim.
branches.stop: Stop generic boundary-as-sampler idea if it offers no gain beyond matched semantic/query-aware selectors on unseen videos or only oracle GT boundaries help.

branches.stage: PROPOSED / NO EXPERIMENT (Oct 27): Separate from CC-09 detection, motivated by IndoML 2026 Track-2 event-aware denoising. Existing public MaskNet baseline already performs SI-SDR training, global clean/mix blending and RMS restoration; ICASSP 2025 LiSenNet already uses a detector for adaptive denoising. Generic noise gating and blending are not novel. Need measure boundary-specific speech preservation at matched enhancement runtime and noise reduction. SOURCE-BASED GENERALIZATION GATE (27 Oct): IndoML organizer says every clip contains a noise event and every clip must be processed by one general enhancement approach; validation-event lookup dictionaries or skipping selected clips are not acceptable competition methods. Evaluate offline hard/soft time-gating only with fully processed waveforms and fair always-on/global-blend controls. Compare speech distortion, SI-SDR, ΔWER by speaker/language, and full detector-plus-enhancer runtime. No waveform study run. ACCEPTED-PRIOR-ART GATE (27 Oct): Interspeech 2025 URGENT challenge already evaluated multilingual speech enhancement and reports language dependence for some generative models. Accepted DeepFilterGAN addresses over-suppression. Do not claim multilingual speech preservation or generic soft gating as a new objective. Compare fixed enhancement outputs with language-stratified WER/damage and hard-gate/global-blend controls. No waveform model test yet. NEW ORGANIZER RULE GATE (Oct 27): IndoML states every challenge clip contains noise and disallows filename/score-triggered bypass or fixed validation-noise dictionaries. For retrospective academic work run the frozen enhancer on every clip and use any uncertainty gate only on its output, with full compute counted; no validation lookup. NEW SOURCE-MATCHING WARNING: ARTPARK Vaani-Benchmark-V1.0 contains multi-reference Hindi ASR tests, not paired synthetic clean/noisy waveforms for SI-SDR and not the IndoML noise-event Gold set. Do not repurpose test-only ASR references for development or claim clean-target speech enhancement scores from them. Original noise-event release requires accepting HF dataset terms; no data access verified.
branches.question: For a fixed frozen speech enhancer and noise detector, can uncertainty-aware soft gating around predicted noise-event boundaries reduce ASR word errors on overlapping multilingual speech at fixed SI-SDR and full runtime relative to always-on enhancement, public global blend, and hard predicted-event gating?
branches.novelty: Very tentative. LiSenNet (ICASSP 2025) already uses a noise detector for adaptive speech enhancement; TQ-SED (ICASSP 2025) already couples audio separation and sound event detection in overlapping events. IndoML 2026 organizer explicitly defines selective noise suppression preserving speech. Distinct claim must be boundary-uncertainty tradeoff under spontaneous multilingual speech with fixed models and prospective independent evaluation; no first-to-combine event detection and enhancement claims. Already-known tradeoffs: Interspeech 2025 URGENT reports multilingual dependence and subjective/discriminative method differences; DeepFilterGAN (Interspeech 2025) studies over-suppression. Only a controlled *event-uncertainty-aware* intervention under frozen enhancer/ASR and matched cost could add new evidence.
branches.pilot: Pin released frozen baseline checkpoint and authorized original recordings. Separate collection-source/recording groups between tune and test; forbid clip-level leakage and lookup of validation noise. Compare same enhancer and ASR with (A) always-on enhancement, (B) baseline global blend, (C) hard event gating, (D) calibrated soft onset/offset transitions; (E) oracle timestamp as explicitly non-deployable upper bound only. Hold total encoder/enhancer/decoder cost, clip set, predicted event inputs and tuning budget constant. On synthetic paired clean/noisy speech report SI-SDR and pooled delta-WER; on genuine field recordings use pooled ASR delta-WER and speech fidelity proxy only, not SI-SDR without clean references. Slice by event overlap/speech, language and unseen noise category. A small CPU-only cached-output development pilot precedes any audio model run. Predeclare multilingual and event-density strata before seeing outcomes. Evaluate always-on, global-blend, hard event-gate, soft uncertainty-gate with identical frozen denoiser output and inference inputs, event boundary uncertainty, matched signal processing + detector runtime. Report SI-SDR, ΔWER, clean-speech distortion and bootstrap intervals by held-out speaker/language. Require a prospectively frozen noninferiority margin for WER in each stratum. No experiment yet.
branches.stop: Stop standalone publication claim if uncertainty-aware gating fails to beat full blended/hard-gate baselines under matched suppression, speech WER, and cost; if gains require oracle test labels, copy/memorize validation noise, or repeat LiSenNet-type adaptive gating without a distinct mechanism; or if no independent clean reference/ASR labels exist for the claimed metrics.

examples.note: Five domains, real heterogeneous multi-source base tasks, generated variants and stage-wise blocking/matching/fusion evaluation. Labeled source pairs do not establish complete true-link clusters; end-to-end reference clustering uses silver labels. Includes one-run-per-task coding-agent pipeline evidence, not reliability across repeated runs.

examples.title: S2AND: A Benchmark and Evaluation System for Author Name Disambiguation (JCDL 2021)
examples.kind: Accepted JCDL 2021 dataset/method paper; public author-signature cluster labels and reference code
examples.note: Eight harmonized real author-name-disambiguation datasets with published cluster evaluation. This is a single bibliographic/corpus and blocking context, not the same as heterogeneous 3-source entity resolution. Check within-block label completeness, singleton treatment, cluster-disjoint splits and data size before a completion-recall claim.

examples.title: GraLMatch: Matching Groups of Entities with Graphs and Language Models (EDBT 2025)
examples.kind: Accepted EDBT 2025 group entity-matching research paper with released code and synthetic multi-source benchmark
examples.note: A strong prior-art baseline for group matching and transitive errors. Real financial-provider records are licensed and not publicly shared; public company/security group datasets use artificial modifications. Do not describe inaccessible real provider data as an available external holdout.

examples.title: An End-To-End Re-Evaluation of Table Entity-Linkers (ICDE 2026)
examples.note: Already measures individual entity-linker components, scalability and reproducibility, identifying candidate generation as a key bottleneck; generic end-to-end or candidate-stage evaluation is NOT a first contribution for CC-04.

examples.title: A precision-driven evaluation protocol for author name disambiguation (Oct 2026)
examples.kind: October 2026 arXiv PREPRINT, not verified accepted
examples.note: Already proposes cluster-level lumping/splitting errors and a combined author-disambiguation evaluation score. CC-04 cannot introduce those metrics as novel; test complete-link allocation separately.

examples.title: DISCERN: Can AI Agents Work Like Scientists and Guide Discovery? (Sep 2026)
examples.kind: September 2026 arXiv PREPRINT; accepted status not verified
examples.note: Already evaluates scientific agents across data-integrity checks, analysis verification and hypotheses under clean/confounded controls. CC-08 general scientific-agent verification has major prior-art overlap; source-revision-specific replay remains unverified.

examples.title: VAANI Noise Event Dataset: A curated spontaneous speech dataset annotated with timestamps for noise events (Sep 2026)
examples.kind: September 2026 arXiv preprint; acceptance not verified
examples.note: Already publishes multilingual Indic speech noise event timestamp corpus and seven event categories. Cannot claim first dataset; no public audio model result from this research cycle.

examples.title: Training Onset-and-Offset-Aware Sound Event Detection on a Heterogeneous Dataset via Probabilistic Sequential Modeling (Interspeech 2025)
examples.note: HSMM onset/offset modeling with heterogeneous clip-level and unlabeled supervision is prior art; generic Gold/Silver/Bronze boundary decoder is insufficient novelty.

examples.title: Exploring Text-Queried Sound Event Detection with Audio Source Separation (ICASSP 2025)
examples.note: Separation-based handling of overlapping audio events and event detection already demonstrated. Do not claim first SED plus separation.

examples.title: LiSenNet: Lightweight Sub-band and Dual-Path Modeling for Real-Time Speech Enhancement (ICASSP 2025)
examples.note: Detector-guided adaptive speech enhancement with low computation exists. Any uncertainty-based soft boundary gating must beat this kind of prior art under matched cost.

examples.title: IndoML 2026 organizer's released two-track baseline code
examples.kind: Public organizer-provided baseline implementation, NOT an accepted paper
examples.note: Already supports tier weighting, onset/offset boundary loss, post-processing sweeps and separation/blending; baseline scorer has a 50 ms minimum collar not explicit in general organizer website text. Verify actual official grader rather than claim discrepancy as measured bug.

examples.title: Sound Event Bounding Boxes (SEBBs) — Interspeech 2024
examples.kind: Accepted Interspeech 2024 method; released SEBBs implementation
examples.note: Already separates predicted event extents from presence confidence and builds event candidates from changes in frame-level predictions. CC-09 must compare with this and Yoshinaga HSMM; generic postprocessing/threshold decoupling is not novel. Evaluation on VAANI has NOT been run.

examples.title: Event-Anchored Frame Selection for Effective Long-Video Understanding (Mar 2026)
examples.kind: March 2026 arXiv preprint; acceptance NOT independently verified
examples.note: Already uses self-supervised visual temporal partitioning, per-event query-aware anchors and MMR for budgeted frames. CC-06 should not claim generic event-anchor selection first; require matched frame and total-compute comparisons against accepted RIDGE.

examples.title: AdaMAE: Adaptive Masking for Efficient Spatiotemporal Learning With Masked Autoencoders (CVPR 2023)
examples.kind: Accepted CVPR 2023, source and method audited; full-video-informed sampler
examples.note: Adaptive learnable visible-token selection is established prior art. Released pretraining code embeds all patches, samples positions from an all-token-conditioned distribution, then passes selected tokens to encoder. Possible mask-index information channel, not a measured failure. Closest accepted baseline for CC-02.

examples.title: Interspeech 2025 URGENT Speech Enhancement Challenge
examples.note: Thirty-two challenge submissions; tests language dependency and speech quality tradeoffs. Generative approaches may be language dependent. CC-17 cannot claim first multilingual speech-preserving enhancement evaluation.

examples.title: DeepFilterGAN: A Full-band Real-time Speech Enhancement System with GAN-based Stochastic Regeneration
examples.note: Studies speech over-suppression and low-latency hybrid enhancement. Controls CC-17 claims about speech preservation and adaptive suppression; not a direct event-gating identical-cost test.

examples.title: Automated Detection of Visual Attribute Reliance with a Self-Reflective Agent
examples.note: Already generates/tests hypotheses and uses iterative self-reflection across 130 models and 18 attribute categories. CC-08 must not claim generic automated self-reflective research verification as novel; version-locked evidence replay remains separate and unverified.

examples.title: Sound Event Detection with Boundary-Aware Optimization and Inference
examples.kind: Accepted IEEE Signal Processing Letters 2026 (DOI 10.1109/LSP.2026.3698771; arXiv v2 confirms accepted status)
examples.note: Schmid et al. train recurrent event detection, onset/offset focal losses and GRU event proposal networks; compare on AudioSet Strong against MF, SEBB, HSM3. Claimed ATST-F AS-Strong-10 collar F1 48.9 vs 42.4 for SEBB in authors' study; not VAANI results and requires retraining model heads. Blocks generic CC-09 learned-boundary and no-postprocessing novelty claims.

examples.title: MLR-Bench: Evaluating AI Agents on Open-Ended Machine Learning Research
examples.kind: Accepted NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (official proceedings)
examples.note: 201 workshop-sourced open-ended ML tasks, modular autonomous research agent and review framework. Authors report frequent fabricated or invalidated experimental outputs for tested coding agents (roughly 80% in cited setting); not this program's measured result and not an estimate for all agents. CC-08 must focus on claim/source-revision/toolchain-exact replay beyond text-based evaluation.

examples.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
examples.kind: 2025 system/preprint and organizer-coordinated reviewer experiment; NO accepted published ICLR workshop paper
examples.note: Sakana AI reports three fully automated ICLR 2025 workshop manuscripts. One scored 6,7,6 in peer review, above a typical workshop threshold, but it was withdrawn before meta-review and publication under a pre-agreed protocol. Cite as reviewer-threshold demonstration, not conference paper acceptance.

examples.title: ReproAgent: Contract-Guided Paper-to-Code Reproduction (Findings EMNLP 2026)
examples.kind: Accepted Findings EMNLP 2026 research paper; public source and experiment artifacts
examples.note: Persistent implementation contract binds paper obligations, file-level evidence, code generation and repair; strong direct prior art against generic contract-based source trace for automated research. Not independently reproduced here.

examples.title: GRACE-DS: Guarded Reward-guided Agent Correction Environment (EMNLP 2026 Industry)
examples.kind: Accepted EMNLP 2026 Industry paper; original authors report thousands of sandboxed trials
examples.note: Already audits hidden-test correctness, leakage, protocol validity and reproducibility with isolated executable validators. Authors report 7,000 episodes; not verified by this scout. Generic sandbox-based AI-agent auditing is not novel.

examples.title: Read the Paper, Write the Code: Agentic Reproduction of Social-Science Results (EMNLP 2026)
examples.note: Already evaluates independent paper-to-code reproduction from original data using information isolation and deterministic cell-level checks on authors' 48-paper benchmark. New CC-08 must demonstrate something beyond this established setup.

examples.title: PILOT: Simulating Failure Recovery In Situ for Production Distributed Systems (NSDI 2026)
examples.note: Already studies in-situ failure-recovery simulation. Different from agent-driven optimization placement variance, but precludes first-to-simulate-failure claims.

examples.title: Speech Event Detector: Timestamped Detection of Non-Verbal Vocalizations and Background Sounds for Rich Speech Transcription (Oct 2026 PREPRINT)
examples.kind: October 9 2026 arXiv preprint, no conference acceptance verified; public code, gated non-commercial checkpoint
examples.note: 54-class 40ms background/speaker event detector already trains on VAANI with six other corpora, label harmonization, and class-wise threshold calibration. Author-selected 14-district VAANI holdout; train/test identity provenance must be audited before comparison to IndoML or treating it as external generalization. Paper Appendix D says exact retraining requires an unreleased 31-class warm-start; final Hub model is gated. No independent model benchmark run.

examples.title: Group-Level Data Selection for Efficient Pretraining (Group-MATES, NeurIPS 2025)
examples.note: Group-level influence-based selection already claims a training efficiency/quality frontier; CC05 cannot claim budgeted subset selection as a new field. Author performance findings are not reproduced here.

examples.title: Computational Budget Should Be Considered in Data Selection (CADS, NeurIPS 2025)
examples.note: Already formulates data selection conditioned on computational budget and studies variation across budgets. CC05 must compare all selection overhead and training within matched total costs rather than claim budget awareness is new.

examples.title: RegMix-D: Dynamic Data Mixing via Proxy Training Trajectories
examples.note: Uses proxy-run trajectories to predict dynamic training mixtures; reduces novelty of generic low-compute dynamic mixture claims. Do not treat author-reported gains as measured in CS Conf.

examples.title: AgentGraph: Trace-to-Graph Platform for Interactive Analysis and Robustness Testing in Agentic AI Systems
examples.kind: AAAI 2026 DEMONSTRATION TRACK; not full main-track research
examples.note: Converts agent logs into linked tool/data/trace graphs and evaluates perturbations/causality. This limits CC08's generic provenance-graph and perturbation claims; it does not prove exact-revision replay.

examples.title: AI Coding Agents Can Reproduce Social Science Findings (SocSci-Repro-Bench)
examples.note: 221 social-science tasks distinguished source-reproducible and missing-material cases; accepted status not established. Underlines need to separate agent reproduction failure from source-artifact incompleteness in CC08.

examples.title: ReplicatorBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Replicability in Social and Behavioral Sciences (KDD 2026)
examples.kind: ACCEPTED/PUBLISHED KDD 2026 proceedings; AI4Sciences track noted in author repository; DOI 10.1145/3770855.3819003
examples.note: Human-verified replicable and non-replicable research claims; agent data retrieval, experimental design and sandbox execution, interpretation, process/outcome evaluation. Related accepted CC08 prior art. Author source https://github.com/CenterForOpenScience/llm-benchmarking/tree/main/replicatorbench requires OpenAI API key for documented full run and Docker, so no free replication assumed. No scout execution.

examples.title: BioAgent Bench: An AI Agent Evaluation Suite for Bioinformatics (ICML 2026)
examples.kind: ACCEPTED ICML 2026 research; PMLR volume 306, pages 28566–28583
examples.note: Manually curated RNA-seq, variant-calling and metagenomics agent tasks; graded outputs and input-corruption, decoy and prompt-bloat robustness tests. Blocks generic new bioinformatics-agent robustness claims in CC08; NOT a substitute for CC12 microscopy lineage metrics. No scout execution.

examples.title: RepLLM: Toward Automatically Reproducing Network Research Results (SIGCOMM 2026)
examples.kind: ACCEPTED SIGCOMM 2026 technical-program paper; author-reported reproduction performance, not reproduced here
examples.note: Four-agent paper-to-network-system-code workflow using content parsing, architecture design, code generation and audit/repair, with sandboxed debugging. Blocks generic automated paper-to-code network-reproduction novelty for CC-08; the original frozen 12-case claim/revision audit remains distinct only if proven by independent replay. 95% reproduction figure in program is the authors' reported metric, not verified by this scout.

examples.title: Verifying Non-Deterministic Convergence on a Global Production WAN (SIGCOMM 2026)
examples.kind: ACCEPTED SIGCOMM 2026 networking experience/research program; TianYan deployment
examples.note: TianYan quantifies routing nondeterminism in production WAN convergence; broad 'network nondeterminism exists' is established prior art. Its WAN routing question differs from CC-13's proposed agent-optimization host-placement and contention paired tests; no scout network measurements.

examples.title: Replication: A Two Decade Review of Policy Atoms — Tracing the Evolution of AS Path Sharing Prefixes (IMC 2025)
examples.kind: ACCEPTED IMC 2025 Replicability Track paper; organizer program and author publication record
examples.note: Revisits a published BGP policy-atom finding using independent later observations, with IPv6 and time-evolution analysis. Confirms accepted replicability scope and shows need for new independent evidence, not an easy/automatic acceptance route. No original data downloaded or new replicate performed.

examples.title: Replication: Characterizing MPLS Tunnels over Internet Paths (IMC 2025)
examples.kind: ACCEPTED IMC 2025 Replicability Track paper; organizer program
examples.note: Replicates earlier MPLS traceroute work using PyTNT and wider contemporary observations; CAIDA describes infrastructure-scale data, not a cheap two-hour reproduction. Illustrates why IMC 2027 EoI must scope independent dataset access and practical budget before any submission.
